title: Glass Bottles on the Kitchen Shelf
description: Explore familiar glass containers through their lids, shapes, colors, and uses in the kitchen.
cardDescription: Explore familiar glass containers through their lids, shapes, colors, and uses in the kitchen.
subtheme: Glass Bottles on the Kitchen Shelf
focus: A bottle has a narrow neck, while a jar usually has a wider opening. These clues use ordinary container words.
solvingTip: Start with the container names before the shape words.
words: Container with a narrow neck for holding a drink
Wide-mouthed container often closed with a screw lid
Clear hard material used to make many bottles
Cover closing the top of a jar
Narrow upper part of a bottle
Easy to see through, as an uncolored glass bottle is
Circular in outline, as a jar's opening is
Even to the touch, as a glass jar's side is
Flat support holding the kitchen containers
Containing nothing, as a used bottle may be
Tip a bottle to let its contents flow out
Clear drink that can be kept in a glass bottle

answerNotes.BOTTLE: A bottle's narrow neck helps guide liquid when it is poured.
answerNotes.JAR: A jar's opening is usually wider than a bottle's neck.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass names the material here, rather than a drinking vessel.
answerNotes.LID: A lid covers the opening and can often be removed completely.
answerNotes.NECK: The neck leads to the bottle's smaller opening.

title: Paper on the Writing Desk
description: Find the sheets, notes, folds, and writing tools beside a stack of ordinary paper.
cardDescription: Find the sheets, notes, folds, and writing tools beside a stack of ordinary paper.
focus: A sheet is one piece of paper. It can become a note or a folded card when someone writes on it.
solvingTip: Try a short writing-tool word before the paper descriptions.
words: Thin material used for a handwritten note
Stack of paper sheets joined along one edge
Short written message on a small piece of paper
Bend a paper sheet so one part lies over another
One side of a sheet in a notebook
Make words on the paper with a pen
Ink-filled tool used to sign a note
Writing tool whose marks can usually be erased
Outside boundary of a paper sheet
Common color of plain writing paper
Printed guide keeping handwriting in a straight row
Even in texture, as some writing paper is
Pile of paper sheets laid one above another

answerNotes.PAPER: Paper is the material; a sheet is an individual piece of it.
answerNotes.SHEET: A sheet has two sides that can be written or printed on.
answerNotes.PAD: A pad keeps sheets together until they are torn or lifted away.
answerNotes.NOTE: A note can be brief without being a complete letter.
answerNotes.FOLD: A fold changes the sheet's shape without cutting away any material.

title: Shaping a Small Clay Bowl
description: Work with a small clay bowl through its round shape, soft material, and hand-shaped sides.
cardDescription: Work with a small clay bowl through its round shape, soft material, and hand-shaped sides.
focus: Soft clay can be pressed into a bowl shape and later fired to become hard. The clues stay with familiar actions and objects.
solvingTip: Begin with a shape, body part, or everyday action.
words: Soft earth material shaped to make this bowl
Deep rounded dish being formed from the soft material
Press the clay between a thumb and finger
Potter's oven used to fire a clay bowl
Coating fired onto pottery to give it a finished surface
Small rounded container made from clay
Containing water, as newly worked clay does
Easy to press with the fingers
Shaped like a circle when viewed from above
Body part used to press and shape the bowl
Give the clay its intended form
Move a lump of clay back and forth under the palm
Lose moisture before the next pottery-making stage
Energy supplied while the pottery is fired

answerNotes.CLAY: Clay can be shaped when moist and made hard by firing.
answerNotes.BOWL: The bowl's sides rise around the space that will hold its contents.
answerNotes.PINCH: Pinching is one simple hand-forming method rather than a turning wheel technique.
answerNotes.KILN: A kiln is made for firing pottery at suitable high temperatures.
answerNotes.GLAZE: Glaze is a surface coating, not the soft clay forming the bowl itself.

title: Wood Viewed Along and Across the Grain
description: Compare wood surfaces through growth rings, knots, and thin layers used in manufactured boards.
cardDescription: Compare wood surfaces through growth rings, knots, and thin layers used in manufactured boards.
subtheme: Wood Viewed Along and Across the Grain
focus: Wood looks different across and along its fibers. The clues distinguish a cut orientation from a growth feature and from a product assembled from thin wood layers.
solvingTip: Use whether the clue describes direction, natural growth, or a manufactured layer.
words: Wood surface cut across the fibers, with spaces omitted
Younger outer wood that conducts water in a tree
Older inner wood formed toward the center of many trunks
Thin layer of wood used as a surface or in layered products
Board made by bonding wood layers with alternating grain directions
Wood feature at the place where a branch joined the trunk
Growth band visible on a crosscut trunk
Outer tree covering removed from many lumber products
Long relatively flat piece of sawn wood
Narrow side of a rectangular board
Broad surface of a sawn board
Cutting tool used to divide timber into pieces
Central material within a layered wood panel
Fibrous material obtained from tree stems
Long substantial member used to support a structure

answerNotes.ENDGRAIN: End grain reveals the cut ends of fibers; it looks different from a lengthwise face.
answerNotes.SAPWOOD: Sapwood is a natural tissue region, not a coating added at a woodworking bench.
answerNotes.HEARTWOOD: Heartwood differs from sapwood in function and often in appearance, though species vary.
answerNotes.VENEER: A veneer is a thin sheet, distinct from a thick solid board.
answerNotes.PLYWOOD: Alternating layer directions help distinguish plywood from a single solid plank.
answerNotes.KNOT: A knot records a growth connection rather than necessarily being a crack or fastening.

title: Familiar Metals and Alloys
description: Compare common metals and their mixtures through familiar material names and manufacturing words.
cardDescription: Compare common metals and their mixtures through familiar material names and manufacturing words.
focus: An alloy combines a metal with other elements. The clues identify traditional compositions while recognizing that modern materials can include additional ingredients and variations.
solvingTip: Use the named combination of elements before choosing a finished-object or process word.
words: Metallic material combining a metal with one or more other elements
Iron-based alloy commonly containing a controlled amount of carbon
Tin-rich alloy used for decorative and household objects
Soft silvery metal forming most traditional pewter
Metal combined with copper to make ordinary brass
Metal forming the principal base of steel
Reddish metal shared by traditional brass and bronze
Silvery metal used in many alloys and coatings
Iron-corrosion product often appearing reddish brown
Natural material from which a useful metal can be extracted
Cast block of metal prepared for later working
To form metal by pouring molten material into a mold

answerNotes.ALLOY: An alloy can include nonmetal elements as well as metals; steel is an example containing carbon.
answerNotes.BRASS: Brass is distinguished from traditional tin bronze by zinc as a principal added element.
answerNotes.BRONZE: Bronze now describes a broader set of copper alloys too; copper and tin identify the classic composition in this clue.
answerNotes.STEEL: Steel differs from pure iron; its properties depend on composition and processing.
answerNotes.PEWTER: Pewter is mainly tin, while additional constituents have varied across periods and products.
